Before entering politics he ran an advertising company, served as mayor of San Salvador, then founded his own party and became president of El Salvador in 2019 — who is he?

Nayib Bukele: President of El Salvador since 2019. Nayib Armando Bukele Ortez (born 24 July 1981) is a Salvadoran politician and businessman who has served as the 43rd president of El Salvador since 2019.
Formed from the union of Deira and Bernicia, this early medieval English kingdom once stretched from the Humber all the way to the Firth of Forth — which kingdom?
Northumbria: Medieval English kingdom. Northumbria was an early medieval English kingdom, existing between 654 and 1066 AD, spanning modern-day Northern England and Southern Scotland.
This Austrian-born SS commando led the Gran Sasso raid that freed Mussolini from captivity and later advised Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser after fleeing to Franco's Spain — who was he?
This British explorer and his eldest son vanished in 1925 hunting an ancient lost city he was convinced lay hidden in the Amazon rainforest — who was he?
Percy Fawcett: British explorer and military officer.
Auguste Comte pioneered this 19th-century philosophy holding that all genuine knowledge comes from logic and sensory experience, dismissing intuition and faith — what is it?
Before serving as Chicago's mayor and later as U.S. ambassador to Japan, this Illinois Democrat was Barack Obama's first White House chief of staff — who is he?
Rahm Emanuel: American politician and diplomat (born 1959)

This American naval aviator and polar explorer discovered Mount Sidley — Antarctica's largest dormant volcano — and claimed to be first to reach both Poles by air, though the North Pole claim remains disputed. Who was he?
Richard E. Byrd: American naval officer (1888–1957)
This August 1992 siege in Boundary County, Idaho began when U.S. Marshals came to arrest Randy Weaver — over a sawed-off shotgun sale — after he was given the wrong court date. What event was it?
Ruby Ridge standoff: 1992 siege and shootout in Idaho, US.
This French explorer crossed the Atlantic some two dozen times, drew the first accurate maps of North America's eastern coast and Great Lakes, and founded Quebec City in 1608. Who was he?
Samuel de Champlain: French explorer of North America (1574–1635)
Born in Leptis Magna in Roman Africa, this general emerged as the final victor of the chaotic Year of the Five Emperors to rule Rome from 193 to 211 — who is he?
Septimius Severus: Roman emperor from 193 to 211. Lucius Septimius Severus (Latin: [ˈluːkius sepˈtimius seˈweːrus]; 11 April 145 – 4 February 211) was Roman emperor from 193 to 211.
Fought in two stages, a winter and summer campaign from 1614 to 1615, this conflict ended the Toyotomi clan and cemented Tokugawa rule over Japan — which historic clash?
Siege of Osaka: 1614-15 series of battles in Japan at the end of the Sengoku Period.
Dubbed the "King of Gambling," this billionaire held a 40-year government monopoly over Macau's casinos and split his fortune among children who run MGM Macau and City of Dreams — who was he?

Ceded by the Qing dynasty after its defeat in an 1895 war with a rising East Asian empire, this island served as that empire's first colony, governed for the next 50 years from a capital called Taihoku — what period of history is this?
Taiwan under Japanese rule: 1895–1945 colony of the Empire of Japan.
Serving as Lord Chancellor before becoming Archbishop of Canterbury, this cleric clashed with King Henry II and was murdered by the king's men in 1170 — who was he?
Thomas Becket: Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 to 1170.
What is this — “1938 spree killing in Japan”?
Tsuyama massacre: 1938 spree killing in Japan. It is the deadliest shooting by a lone gunman in Japanese history.
This French Romantic giant gave the world both 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame' and a sprawling 1862 novel that became a beloved musical — who was he?
Victor Hugo: French writer and politician (1802–1885)
Nicknamed the "Land Cruiser War," this conflict erupted in Sudan in 2003 and led to President Omar al-Bashir being indicted for genocide by the International Criminal Court. What was it?
War in Darfur: Genocidal conflict in Western Sudan.
Also known as the Prince of Orange, he led the Dutch revolt against Spanish Habsburg rule that ignited the Eighty Years' War and eventually won the United Provinces their independence — who is he?
William the Silent: Dutch revolt leader (1533–1584)

Born to a family of strawberry farmers in Akita Prefecture, this politician rose to become Japan's Prime Minister from 2020 to 2021 after years as Chief Cabinet Secretary under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Yoshihide Suga: Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021. Yoshihide Suga (菅 義偉, Suga Yoshihide; born 6 December 1948) is a Japanese former politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021.
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Anna Atkins (born 1799) is the earliest of the four. Anna Atkins (née Children; 16 March 1799 – 9 June 1871) was an English botanist and photographer.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below was established earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Paul Ehrenfest is a physicist. Suffering from depression, in 1933 Ehrenfest killed his disabled son, Wassik, and then himself.
Which of these is a chemist?
Karen Silkwood is a chemist. The company settled out of court for US$1.38 million, while not admitting liability.
What is the atomic number of Magnesium?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
In what year was Jean Tatlock born?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year was Guglielmo Marconi born?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year was Sam Altman born?
Sam Altman: Altman attended Stanford University for two years before he dropped out and co-founded Loopt, a smartphone geosocial networking service.
In what year did Ernest Lawrence die?
Ernest Lawrence: A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Coriolis force discovered?
Coriolis force: In physics, the Coriolis force is a pseudo-force that acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Methotrexate: Pfizer. Methotrexate, formerly known as amethopterin, is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Which country is Bombardier Global Express from?
Bombardier Global Express: Canada. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.
Who is credited with discovering Infrared?
Infrared: William Herschel. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Who is credited with discovering Cherenkov radiation?
Cherenkov radiation: Sergey Vavilov. A classic example of Cherenkov radiation is the characteristic blue glow of an underwater nuclear reactor.
Who is credited with discovering Argon?
Argon: William Ramsay. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.

A central nervous system stimulant of the phenethylamine class, this combo medication is approved for narcolepsy and ADHD — but is also taken as an appetite suppressant and cognitive enhancer. What is it?
Adderall is the brand name of a fixed-dose combination medication used for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
These organic compounds, formed when one or more hydrogens in ammonia are replaced by carbon-based groups, are defined by their carbon-nitrogen bonds — what's this class of compounds called?
Amine (UK also) are organic compounds that contain carbon-nitrogen bonds.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
This British mathematician coined the term 'mathematical induction' and is best remembered for a pair of laws linking conjunction, disjunction, and negation in logic — who was he?
Augustus De Morgan (27 June 1806 - 18 March 1871) was a British mathematician and logician.
Usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky, this red supergiant in the constellation Orion varies noticeably in brightness over a roughly 400-day cycle — name the star?
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion. Its Bayer designation is α Orionis, Latinised to Alpha Orionis and abbreviated Alpha Ori or α Ori.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.

Native to Madagascar and grown as an ornamental tree throughout the tropics, this legume species has fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red flowers; its wild origin wasn't confirmed until 1932. What tree is this?
Delonix regia is a species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae, subfamily Caesalpinioideae native to Madagascar.

This American entrepreneur co-founded Facebook alongside Mark Zuckerberg, then left in 2008 to co-found the productivity company Asana, becoming the youngest self-made billionaire in the world by 2011 — who is he?

Dustin Moskovitz (born May 22, 1984) is an American internet entrepreneur who co-founded the social media service Facebook and its parent company Meta Platforms with Mark Zuckerberg, Eduardo Saverin, Andrew McCollum and Chris Hughes.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.
Immature at birth but developed by puberty, this network of organs includes the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes, protected by a fold called the labia majora — what's it called?
Female reproductive system is made up of the internal and external sex organs that function in the reproduction of new offspring.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, feeds only on blood, and has legs too short and stumpy to jump or even walk well on a flat surface — what is it?
Head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) is an obligate ectoparasite of humans.
While first described from Virginia, this genus of flowering shrubs reaches its greatest diversity in East Asia, and some species climb up to 30 metres by scaling trees. What plant is it?
Hydrangea (or) is a genus of more than 70 species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
A former Chicago financial options trader, this internet entrepreneur co-founded a nonprofit free encyclopedia as well as the for-profit wiki host Fandom — who is he?
Jimmy Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.
Her women's absolute land speed record stood until 2019, she got her own action figure, and Google honored her with a Doodle in 2023 — this deaf stuntwoman and racer. Who is she?
Kitty O'Neil ((1946-03-24)March 24, 1946 - (2018-11-02)November 2, 2018) was an American stuntwoman and auto-racer, often called "the fastest woman in the world" for her various speed records.
This American computer scientist rose to prominence after Elon Musk praised his MIT study on Tesla's semi-autonomous driving system, and now hosts a long-form interview podcast. Who is he?
Lex Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.
Enclosed in a fibrous capsule and linked throughout the body by lymphatic vessels, these kidney-shaped organs filter foreign particles and house the immune system's B and T cells — what are they?
Lymph node is a kidney-shaped organ of the lymphatic system and the adaptive immune system.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
Carrying the NATO reporting name 'Halo,' this Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter is the largest of its kind ever to enter serial production — name the aircraft?
Mil Mi-26 is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Likened to insulation on an electrical wire, this fatty material sheaths axon segments to speed up the transmission of nerve impulses — what is it called?

Myelin is a lipid-rich material that in most vertebrates surrounds the axons of neurons to insulate them and increase the rate at which electrical impulses (called action potentials) pass along the axon.

Born in New York to Jewish Holocaust-survivor parents, this Princeton-trained political scientist studies the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — and his 2007 DePaul tenure fight made headlines. Who is he?
Norman Finkelstein (born December 8, 1953) is an American political scientist and activist.

This female reproductive gland produces eggs that travel through the oviduct to the uterus, while also functioning as an endocrine organ that secretes hormones governing the menstrual cycle — what organ is it?
Ovary (from Latin vrium 'egg') is a gonad in the female reproductive system that produces ova; when released, an ovum travels through the oviduct into the uterus.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

Native to North American grasslands, these burrowing, herbivorous ground squirrels come in five species, black-tailed, white-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah, and Mexican. Name this genus, Cynomys, by its common two-word name?
Prairie dog (genus Cynomys) are herbivorous burrowing ground squirrels native to the grasslands of North America.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
A Jesuit priest, poet, and diplomat from the Republic of Ragusa, this polymath produced an early precursor of atomic theory and in 1753 discovered the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich (18 May 1711 - 13 February 1787) was a physicist, astronomer, mathematician, philosopher, diplomat, poet, theologian, Jesuit priest, and a polymath from the Republic of Ragusa.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and numbering over 2,500 species, this eight-legged arachnid curves a stinger-tipped tail over its back — what is it?

Scorpion (order Scorpiones) are predatory arachnids with eight legs, a pair of grasping pincers (or Chelae) and a narrow, segmented tail, often carried in a characteristic forward curve over the back and always ending with a stinger.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body comes in three main forms — a rigid outer shell, a rigid inner frame, or a flexible fluid-supported structure — what is it called?
Skeleton is the structural frame that supports the body of most animals.
Also known as sea stars, roughly 1,900 species of these star-shaped marine invertebrates live on seabeds from warm tropics to icy polar oceans. What are they?
Starfish are a class of marine invertebrates generally shaped like a star polygon.
Appointed a government economic minister in 1991, this academic rose to become prime minister of Turkey in 1993 and later served as its foreign minister — who is she?
Tansu Çiller (born 24 May 1946) is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This slender, short-legged predator's genus also includes polecats, stoats, and ferrets, and its smallest species is the tiniest carnivore on Earth — what animal is it?
Weasel are mammals of the genus Mustela of the family Mustelidae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Also called the yellow-legged predatory wasp, this insect — native to parts of Southeast Asia — has become an invasive concern across much of Europe — which species?
Asian hornet: Species of insect. The Asian hornet (Vespa velutina), also known as the yellow-legged hornet or Asian predatory wasp, is a species of hornet indigenous to Southeast Asia.
Instead of teeth, these marine mammals sieve plankton through whalebone plates in their mouths — a group of 16 species that includes the rorquals and the bowhead. What do we call them?
A red supergiant in Orion so vast that, placed at the Sun's position, it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, this variable star is designated Alpha Orionis — which star?
Betelgeuse: Red supergiant star in the constellation Orion. It is usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky and, after Rigel, the second brightest in its constellation.

Commonly called the Triple Seven, this American wide-body airliner is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airplane. It was designed to bridge the gap between the twin-engined 767 and quad-engined 747. What is it?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.

Convicted in 2013 for leaking nearly 750,000 classified documents to WikiLeaks while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, this whistleblower had her sentence commuted by President Obama in 2017 — who is she?
Chelsea Manning: American activist and whistleblower (born 1987)
A political scientist studying voter turnout and race, this scholar rose through Harvard's deanships to become its 30th president in 2023 — only to resign months later; who is she?
Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".

Published in 1750 by a mathematician who described it for any number of unknowns, this linear algebra formula solves systems of equations using determinants of the coefficient matrix — what's it called?
Cramer's rule: Formula for systems of linear equations.
Known as the "grandfather of behavioral economics," this psychologist developed prospect theory with Amos Tversky and won the 2002 Nobel in economics — who was he?
Daniel Kahneman: Israeli-American psychologist and economist (1934–2024)
Named from the Latin word for 'finger' and best known through the common foxglove species, which plant genus produces tall spikes of tubular, often purple flowers?
Digitalis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae.

Historically nicknamed 'the bloody flux,' this type of gastroenteritis is usually caused by Shigella bacteria or a parasitic amoeba and spreads through contaminated food and water — what is this illness?
Dysentery: Intestinal inflammation causing bloody diarrhea.
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.
Born in ancient Pergamon to a wealthy architect, this Roman-era Greek physician's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology for centuries — who was he?
Galen: Greek physician, surgeon, and philosopher (c. 129–216 AD)
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this bird of prey hunts either by dashing suddenly from a hidden perch or by pouncing down on prey from open skies — what raptor is it?
Hawk: Bird of prey. The subfamily Accipitrinae includes goshawks, sparrowhawks, sharp-shinned hawks, and others.
Its name means 'river horse' in Ancient Greek, yet this semiaquatic sub-Saharan giant — the largest even-toed ungulate alive — is more closely tied to pigs than to horses; what is it?
Hippopotamus: Species of large semi-aquatic mammal.
This huge insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, and its females often carry an egg-laying tube that doubles as a stinger — what order is it?
Hymenoptera: Order of insects. Over 150,000 living species of Hymenoptera have been described, in addition to over 2,000 extinct ones.
Fever, sore throat, body aches and fatigue that start one to four days after exposure and may spiral into pneumonia — there are four types of this viral infection. What is it?

Alongside Francis Crick, which American biologist co-proposed the double-helix structure of DNA in a 1953 Nature paper, building on the work of Rosalind Franklin, earning a share of the 1962 Nobel Prize?
This French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and a crater on the Moon is named after him; who was he?
The largest joint in the human body, it's a modified hinge that links the thigh to the lower leg via two separate joints — what is it?
Knee: Leg joint in primates. The knee is a modified hinge joint, which permits flexion and extension as well as slight internal and external rotation.

An Atlanta factory superintendent with a Cornell engineering degree, he was wrongly convicted of murdering a young employee, then kidnapped from prison and lynched — a case that became a focus of antisemitism. Who was he?
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.

Captured by Einstein's famous equation E=mc², this principle shows that a tiny amount of one physical quantity converts into an enormous amount of another thanks to the speed of light being squared — what is this relationship called?
Mass–energy equivalence: Physics concept expressed as E = mc².
Aristotle called it the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes existence itself, what all things have in common, and how reality is divided into categories of being. Which field is it?
Marketed under names like Rogaine and Loniten, this medication treats high blood pressure but is best known over-the-counter for combating hair loss — what's the drug?
Minoxidil: Medication to treat high blood pressure and alopecia.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach, this rare-earth element tarnishes quickly in air and produces pink, purple, and yellow compounds when oxidized — which element, atomic number 60?
Neodymium: Chemical element with atomic number 60 (Nd)
This facial organ houses the nares, connects to the humidity-regulating paranasal sinuses, and serves as an alternate airway for nursing infants — which body part?
Nose: Organ that smells and facilitates breathing.
First domesticated in China's Yangtze River basin more than 8,000 years ago, this grass species is the world's most widely cultivated rice — which species?
Oryza sativa: Species of plant. Oryza sativa belongs to the genus Oryza and the BOP clade in the grass family Poaceae.
Defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond, this unit equals about 3.26 light-years — which unit?
Parsec: Unit of length in astronomy.
Featuring an R−O−O−R backbone where two oxygen atoms bond directly to each other, what name covers this class of molecules?
Peroxide: Chemical compounds with the structure R–O–O–R'
Resembling a round, tailless rabbit with short ears, this small mountain-dwelling mammal's Himalayan relative lives at elevations above 6,000 meters — what animal is it?
Pika: Genus of mountain-dwelling mammal. A pika ( PY-kə, PEE-kə) is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
This succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae has every part edible, whether raw or cooked, and is also known by folk names like little hogweed — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Portulaca oleracea: Species of plant in the purslane family.

This noncontagious autoimmune disease shows up as dry, scaly red or purple patches, and injuring the skin can trigger new lesions right at that spot — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon — what is it?
Psoriasis: Autoimmune diseases of the skin. Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.
